headline: Tanker struck by two unidentified projectiles 50nm north of Qatar's Madinat ash Shamal'
dek: [CONFIRMED -- advisory issuance] UKMTO says a tanker was struck by two unidentified projectiles about 50 nautical miles (92.6km) north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar, at 23:20 GMT Wednesday Nov 4; crew status and extent of damage remain unconfirmed; vessels advised to transit with caution while…
sources: UKMTO (United Kingdom Maritime Trade Operations) advisory, relayed by Al Jazeera liveblog, Jerusalem Post and APA
fault_line: Who is hitting Gulf tankers now -- and if a strike can land 50 miles off Qatar with no one named, is any Gulf transit safe?

sections.what_happened: [CONFIRMED -- advisory issuance] UKMTO says a tanker was struck by two unidentified projectiles about 50 nautical miles (92.6km) north of Madinat ash Shamal, Qatar, at 23:20 GMT Wednesday Nov 4; crew status and extent of damage remain unconfirmed; vessels advised to transit with caution while authorities investigate. [UNVERIFIED] Attacker identity, vessel name/flag, weapon type and damage are NOT stated by UKMTO or any relay. [CONTEXT -- AJ economy reel Nov 3] Al Jazeera reports 6 commercial vessels under fire in Gulf/Hormuz waters in 72 hours to Nov 3: Qatari LNG carrier Al Mayeda (Oct 30, already recorded 1500-01 Nov 1), oil tanker 'Large Um' (two missiles, Oct 31), naval tug 'Seal Storm' (projectile west of Musandam, Nov 1), plus 'Riti', 'Arzne' and 'Louis 1'. [COUNTED CONTEXT -- AJ mirror Nov 5 07:10Z] More than 120 commercial ships have been hit in the region since the war began, per IMO/UKMTO data. PORTWATCH BACKBONE: newest snapshot remains portwatch-2026-10-26.json, stale=true (latest observation 2026-10-18: Hormuz 4 transits, 7-day avg 3.71 vs 2025 baseline 85.53/day) -- cited ONLY as stale; PortWatch tracks chokepoints, not Gulf waters off Qatar, so NO counted figure exists for this incident's waters -- record the gap, do not present any claimant number as counted. CAUTION -- NEAR-IDENTICAL LOCATION: an Oct 8 incident (51nm north of Madinat ash Shamal, casualties reported) is a DIFFERENT, earlier event; do not conflate it with this Nov 4 incident.
sections.what_verified: UKMTO is itself the primary source (T1 official); Al Jazeera (T2) and Jerusalem Post (T3) relay the same UKMTO advisory verbatim; APA relayed it but holds NO declared tier in the registry and does not count toward corroboration. The advisory's existence is multi-family confirmed; the incident details beyond the advisory are single-source (UKMTO).
sections.what_disputed: No vessel named, no flag state, insurer or tracker has corroborated the strike; UKMTO itself says it cannot confirm the source of the projectiles and continues to investigate (per the parallel Nov 3 Ras Laffan/Lima reporting). No party has claimed the attack. The Nov 3 engine-room strike (14nm NE of Lima, Oman, no casualties) and this Nov 4 Qatar strike are separate incidents; do not merge their casualty/damage details.
sections.why_matters: A tanker was hit by two projectiles off Qatar overnight -- UKMTO confirms the strike, names no ship and no attacker. Sixth vessel in a week of Gulf attacks; the who and the ship are still blank.
sections.context: Background: MISSED CATCH-UP + IN-WINDOW PUBLICATION (event Nov 4 23:20 UTC = 03:20 Nov 5; AJ liveblog entry 08:27 GMT = 12:27 ; JPost update 10:32 Israel = 11:32 ; APA 12:39 ) -- UKMTO: tanker struck by two unidentified projectiles 50nm north of Qatar's Madinat ash Shamal; crew status and damage unconfirmed

totw_analysis: Our read: A tanker was hit by two projectiles off Qatar overnight -- UKMTO confirms the strike, names no ship and no attacker. Sixth vessel in a week of Gulf attacks; the who and the ship are still blank. The fault line our audience is arguing over: Who is hitting Gulf tankers now -- and if a strike can land 50 miles off Qatar with no one named, is any Gulf transit safe?
